newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday September 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday September 24.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says there will be no government crisis over the 1997 budget (all).

* Public works minister and former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro says there was no special treatment in favour of Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia, a banker who is now jailed in corruption probe along with state railway managing director Lorenzo Necci. In a 1993 inquiry, Pacini Battaglia was arrested by Milan magistrates and then freed after 10 hours (all).

*In a meeting with the majority party leaders, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said public deficit is higher than expected and the 1997 budget should now contain 40 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures instead of planned 32 trillion (all).
* An additional "super-tax" might be introduced next spring to push the public debt towards Maastricht criteria (all).

* September consumer price index in six sample cities was above forecasts (between 0.1 pct and 1 pct), but according to Confindustria's Guidalberto Guidi "there's no reason to think prices won't go down again" (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
